sentence_stem: By the time the train arrives,
correct_completion: we will have been waiting for over two hours.
full_sentence: By the time the train arrives, we will have been waiting for over two hours.
acceptable_variants: we will have been standing here for ages.
we will have spent the whole afternoon on this platform.

options.text: we have been waiting for over two hours.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect continuous looks back from now, but 'by the time' with a future clause needs a future perfect form looking forward to a later moment.

options.text: we will wait for over two hours.
options.why_wrong: The simple future does not express the duration that will be complete at the moment the train arrives, which the future perfect continuous shows.

options.text: we will have been waiting for over two hours.
we were waiting for over two hours.
options.why_wrong: The past continuous refers to the past, but the sentence describes a duration that will be completed in the future.

grammar_focus: Future perfect continuous with 'by the time' for duration up to a future point
explanation: The clause 'by the time the train arrives' places a future reference point, so the main clause needs the future perfect continuous to show a duration that will still be ongoing at that point. Ukrainian speakers often rely on a simple future form here, because Ukrainian verb aspect does not map neatly onto English perfect and continuous forms.
translation: Коли потяг прибуде, ми будемо чекати вже понад дві години.
